create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant validation is documented around signature, issuer, audience/domain, and expiry, but not one-time-use or jti replay prevention.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same JWT assertion may be accepted by design for stateless validation; do not report as replay vulnerability without explicit one-time-use semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An active token can appear inactive to an out-of-audience introspection client; this is by design, not token invalidation.

oidc_jwt.description: Certain reserved scopes intentionally add project identifiers to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Audience expansion caused by requested reserved scopes is expected behavior and should not be flagged as over-issuance.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope that is a subset of the originally granted scope; omitting scope reuses the original scope.
oidc_jwt.note: A rejected refresh request with broader scope is expected behavior, not privilege-loss or privilege-escalation confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange responses may contain scopes that differ from the provided scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: The oracle must compare returned scope and claims to upstream authorization intent and policy, not assume exact echo of the requested scope.

oidc_jwt.description: By default, access-token aud includes all client IDs and the project ID, with optional additional project audiences via reserved scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Multiple audience values are normal and should not be flagged unless they exceed documented defaults plus requested audience scopes.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization-specific reserved scopes intentionally enforce organization membership and may fail authentication if the organization does not exist or the user is not a member.
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failures under these scopes are expected policy enforcement, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes rather than a fixed schema.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile/roles in userinfo is expected when the corresponding scopes were not granted.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint only returns claims permitted by the granted scopes; many profile fields may be absent even for a valid authenticated session.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity verification should rely primarily on sub and only expect optional claims when the corresponding scopes were granted.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion MUST include exp in the future and iat no older than 1 hour. ZITADEL documents that iat MUST NOT be older than 1h, and it verifies that the JWT is not expired. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside attack assertions to distinguish platform rejection from broken test setup.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; jwt_idp.mdx validation notes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT header MUST carry kid matching the configured/downloaded key ID. ZITADEL requires kid to identify the key; missing or wrong kid can fail before signature-trust logic is exercised, confounding alg/key-substitution tests.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer/audience validation tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT claims MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain and iss/sub matching the service account or application identifier from the downloaded key material. Otherwise failures may be due to malformed client assertion/grant construction rather than the intended validation oracle.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For start_oidc_auth, redirect_uri matching is exact. A valid control request MUST use a preregistered redirect_uri byte-for-byte; any mismatch is expected to fail with invalid_grant/authorization failure and is not an I3 bug unless the SAME authorization request is evaluated inconsistently.

For OIDC authorization-code flows, state SHOULD be sent and preserved end-to-end. I3 flow-coherence tests MUST bind each authorize request to its own state and compare callback state values; do not treat missing state protection in your client harness as a platform bug.

For OIDC implicit-flow or request/response tests involving id_token replay, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended generally. I2/I3 tests MUST include nonce on start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token corresponds to that nonce; otherwise replay/confusion results are uninterpretable.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx authorization_endpoint additional parameters; claims.mdx nonce

oidc_jwt.constraint: For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method supports only S256. Do not send other methods expecting a downgrade oracle; unsupported methods are by-design invalid setup. For pkce_skip tests, use a valid authorize request with code_challenge and then omit code_verifier only at token exchange.

For exchange_code_for_token, session_token MUST be taken from access_token, not id_token. ZITADEL userinfo requires the access token of the user as Bearer token; using id_token for verify_granted_identity will fail for the wrong reason.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design and should be used as the negative oracle; do not interpret such failures as setup bugs.

For token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented token type matrix: refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token/actor_token/requested_token_type; JWT subject_token is allowed only with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Use only supported combinations for controls, otherwise failures are by design.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope may be rejected if invalid or if it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. A valid I5 test should compare exchanged-token claims/scope against the original authorization and requested scope, not assume every broader scope request must succeed.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. I5 audience tests using introspection MUST authenticate as an in-audience client for the control case; otherwise active=false can be caused by caller-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication requirements are endpoint-specific and documented as depending on the authorization method. Tests that call these endpoints MUST supply valid client authentication for the control path; a 401 invalid_client is not evidence about token validity or revocation semantics.

For reserved-scope audience tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project id to the access-token audience, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud adds the ZITADEL project id. I5 audience controls MUST account for these scope-driven audience expansions before flagging overbroad audience acceptance.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership by design. Do not combine these scopes with multi-identity I4 collision tests unless the identities are intentionally within the same organization constraint.

For JWT replay tests against login_with_jwt, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as an I2 vulnerability based solely on lack of jti tracking. The provided documentation describes stateless JWT validation properties (signature, issuer, expiry) but does not document one-time-use or jti replay prevention for JWT bearer grants.
oidc_jwt.source: jwt_idp.mdx validation notes; grant-types.mdx JWT Profile

oidc_jwt.constraint: For JWT IdP-style browser SSO flows, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header and the proxy must preserve all original query parameters when forwarding to ZITADEL. Any test of flow coherence or header-injection must distinguish between by-design header transport requirements and acceptance of attacker-controlled headers from untrusted clients.

For OIDC relying-party validation strategy, ZITADEL documentation explicitly ties nonce to replay mitigation and exact redirect_uri matching, and JWT IdP docs state issuer and expiry are verified. Therefore I2/I3 tests MUST include a valid control authorize/token flow with nonce, exact redirect_uri, and a non-expired token before concluding that an attack token was rejected for security reasons.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include time claims relative to now: use iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for control tokens, and expired/future variants for attack tokens. ZITADEL documents that JWT profile assertions MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and token validation also checks that the JWT is not expired. Always run a CONTROL login alongside the ATTACK login so LOGIN_FAILED is not misread as broken setup.

For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests on JWT IdP / JWT profile style JWT validation, the JWT aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} / issuer domain) and the iss claim MUST match the configured issuer when issuer validation is in play. A wrong audience or missing issuer-domain audience causes rejection for the wrong reason and invalidates issuer/key-substitution conclusions.

For I1 kid/key-selection tests, JWTs used with ZITADEL private-key JWT or JWT profile flows MUST carry a kid header identifying the configured keyId. Missing kid can fail key lookup before the intended malicious-key or kid-injection condition is exercised.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and code-binding tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires an exact match; a mismatch yields invalid_grant/authorization failure for normal protocol reasons, not a coherence bug.

For I3 PKCE-related authorization-code tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do NOT send plain or other methods when testing code/session binding unless the goal is specifically to confirm rejection of unsupported methods. Otherwise failures are caused by unsupported PKCE configuration, not by the attack under test.

For I3 pkce_skip/code_injection/state-swap style tests, if start_oidc_auth included PKCE then exchange_code_for_token MUST include the matching code_verifier for control requests. Omitting code_verifier after sending a code_challenge causes expected rejection and cannot be used as evidence of identity/session confusion.

For OIDC authorization requests, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory, while nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. For I3 state-swap tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly send a distinct state per browser session; absence of state removes the binding signal and makes the test meaningless. For I2 replay tests involving id_tokens from implicit flow, nonce MUST be present and checked.

For OIDC implicit-flow tests, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as MUST for implicit flow and returns it in the id_token when provided in the authorization request. Missing nonce can cause rejection or remove replay-binding semantics, so do not use nonce-less implicit requests as attack evidence.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange.audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If you request an audience outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug. Use a control exchange with a valid subset audience first, then vary only the target audience under test.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh or token exchange MUST be interpreted relative to prior authorization: refresh_token scope must be a subset of the original scope, and token exchange may return scopes differing from the request. The fuzzer MUST compare returned scope/claims against upstream authorization intent, not merely whether the request was accepted.

For I5 token exchange token-type tests, only documented token type combinations are valid. In particular, subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type=jwt is only valid in the documented combinations. Do not treat rejection of unsupported token-type combinations as an authorization-binding bug.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL by design includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud by default, and additional project audiences can be added via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or ...:zitadel:aud. The fuzzer MUST account for these default and scope-added audiences before flagging overbroad audience results.

For I5 org-binding tests using reserved scopes, requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} intentionally enforces organization membership and may fail if the org does not exist or the username/domain does not match. Such failures are by design and must not be interpreted as unrelated auth bugs.

For I1/I5 introspection-based verification, introspection only returns active=true when the requesting client is authorized and is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST use an appropriate client context for introspection; otherwise active=false/401 can result from client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity or revocation.

For I2 replay_same_token on login_with_jwt, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same JWT profile assertion as a vulnerability unless the documentation explicitly promises one-time use. The provided docs describe stateless JWT validation requirements (signature, issuer, expiry) but do not document jti replay tracking for JWT profile grants.

For JWT IdP browser-mediated flows, the upstream JWT MUST be delivered in the configured HTTP header and the proxy MUST preserve all original query parameters when forwarding to ZITADEL's JWT receiving endpoint. Missing query parameters breaks OIDC flow state and causes false I3 failures unrelated to JWT validation.

For JWT IdP tests, do NOT place the JWT in a URL parameter. ZITADEL documentation explicitly requires header transport and describes the JWT as extracted from a configured HTTP header. URL-based injection tests would not exercise the documented acceptance path and any rejection is expected.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss equal to sub, and a kid header identifying the registered key. Failures without these fields are invalid setup, not freshness enforcement.

For JWT bearer assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template times relative to now (for control tokens use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}). Tokens older than 1 hour are rejected by design and cannot distinguish exp/nbf enforcement from stale-iat rejection.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT assertion (exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, aud=issuer-domain, iss=sub). Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken key registration or malformed assertion setup.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and code-flow coherence tests, the redirect_uri sent to /oauth/v2/token MUST match exactly the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design.
For OIDC authorization requests, redirect_uri must match exactly one preregistered redirect URI. Do not treat redirect_uri validation failures as state/nonce/PKCE security findings.
For OIDC implicit-flow or request patterns involving id_token issuance from /oauth/v2/authorize, nonce MUST be provided. Missing nonce in implicit flow is invalid setup, not a replay-defense bypass.

For OIDC code-flow tests, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory. A missing state parameter should not be reported as a platform vulnerability unless the test specifically targets client-side CSRF protections outside broker scope.
For PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send plain or alternative methods and interpret rejection as a security issue; unsupported methods are by design.

For OIDC code-flow tests using PKCE, the token request must send the original code_verifier and client_id so ZITADEL can recompute the code_challenge. Missing code_verifier in a PKCE flow is expected to fail and should be asserted via non-200/error status, not identity comparison.

For I1/I2 OIDC RP-style tests, ZITADEL documentation states nonce is used to bind the client session with the ID token and mitigate replay attacks. Therefore start_oidc_auth SHOULD include nonce whenever an id_token is expected, and tests must verify returned nonce only in ID token contexts, not userinfo.

For token_exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token type matrix: subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; subject_token_type=jwt is allowed only with actor_token; user_id subject tokens are allowed only with actor_token. Unsupported combinations must not be reported as security findings.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare requested scope against the returned scope field and returned token claims. ZITADEL documents that returned scopes may differ from requested scope on token and token-exchange responses, so the oracle must inspect actual returned scope/claims rather than assume echo semantics.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. An active=false or authorization failure from a non-audience client is by design and must not be interpreted as token invalidity alone.

For revocation and introspection tests, these endpoints require client authentication by either client_secret_basic, body client_id/client_secret where documented, or private_key_jwt. A 401 invalid_client reflects client-auth failure, not token-state behavior.

For JWT bearer login_with_jwt tests, replay of the same JWT assertion is not documented as prevented via jti tracking. Treat replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti as hardening checks only, not vulnerabilities, unless documentation explicitly adds one-time-use semantics for this grant.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL documents that by default all client IDs and the project ID are included in aud, and additional project audiences can be added via reserved scopes. Do not assume a single audience value when evaluating audience broadness or mismatch.

For userinfo-based identity verification, claims returned depend on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/phone/address/metadata/roles claims without corresponding scopes is by design; only sub is always expected at userinfo.

For I5 reserved-scope tests, requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership and may fail login if the user is not a member or the org does not exist. Such failures are expected scope-enforcement behavior, not authentication bugs.

For I5 audience-expansion tests, adding scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud intentionally adds project IDs to the access-token audience. Do not flag these extra audiences as overbroad when they were explicitly requested.

For JWT IdP browser-flow testing through ZITADEL as RP, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header to /idps/jwt via a proxy that preserves all original query parameters. Sending the JWT as a URL parameter or dropping query parameters breaks OIDC flow state and is invalid test setup.

For JWT IdP validation tests, ZITADEL documents verification of signature using the configured keys endpoint, issuer equality on iss, and expiration. Tests for trust-anchor substitution, kid/key attacks, and issuer substitution MUST configure the JWT IdP with a keys endpoint and issuer first; otherwise failures or acceptances are not attributable to the intended invariant.

For JWT IdP and external OIDC provider tests, ZITADEL may force minimum scopes: generic OIDC always sends at least openid; Entra ID always sends at least openid and User.Read. Do not interpret extra upstream scopes added by ZITADEL as scope-escalation bugs in downstream tokens without checking documented provider defaults.

For end-session/logout tests, post_logout_redirect_uri is ignored unless id_token_hint or client_id is provided, and if both are provided they must be equal by azp/client_id binding. Redirect behavior without those parameters is by design and not a session-management flaw.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
